newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GRABOPLAST UP ON H1 EARNINGS.
newsitem.headline: GRABOPLAST UP ON H1 EARNINGS.

text.p: Shares in Hungarian home improvement product maker Graboplast Rt bucked a bearish trend on the bourse and traded firmer on Wednesday with good first half results as a driving factor, traders said.
Other companies which released their earnings on Wednesday, traded mixed, influenced mainly by tight liquidity, traders said.
"Graboplast's price already reflected expectations but when (results) news comes out, it gives another boost," said Pal Merkovszky of OTP Securities.
Graboplast released its first half consolidated earnings report on Tuesday after the bourse's close.

It said its operating profits rose to 1.062 billion forints in the first half of 1997 from 719.9 million in the first half of 1996, while its after-tax profit rose to 1.097 billion forints from 423.1 million.
Graboplast opened at 12,100 forints and jumped to 12,250 in early trade. At 1010 GMT it traded at 12,200 forints, up 200 from Tuesday's close.
"I see a clear link between Graboplast's earnings and the rise in its shares," said Tamas Revesz of Wintrust, adding the group's earnings were above expectations.
Revesz added, however, that by the end of play the market's bearish sentiment might weigh on Graboplast shares as well.

Among other companies that published first half figures on Wednesday, alcoholic beverages producer Zwack traded firmer, while liquified petroleum gas distributor Primagaz moved lower, both in thin volume.

Zwack opened at 4,600 forints, up from Tuesday's close of 4,150 and at 0947 GMT traded at 4,550. Primagaz opened at 11,030 forints, below Tuesday's close of 11,300, and at 0958 GMT traded at 10,950, down 350.
